messages:
maria-sales: Quick sync 1: MediSure POC goes live tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Legal needs a one-page capacity & price appendix for the SOW. They gave traffic shape: bursty peaks to ~900 RPS for a few minutes, sustained 95th ~600 RPS, avg ~60 tokens per convo. HIPAA required (Private). Asking: what reserved GPU commitment should we propose, and recommended autoscale/burst settings?

ashwin-eng: TL;DR calc: 60 tok/req * 900 RPS = 54k tok/s peak. On current redwood-3-small quantized we measure ~12k tok/s per GPU under 95th latency targets, so peak capacity ~54k/12k = 4.5 -> round up to 5 GPUs if you want headroom for brief peaks.

jordan-ml: If customer will accept aggressive quantization + KV caching we see ~15k tok/s/GPU. In that case 4 GPUs could handle peaks with preheat + warm KV. Note: quality tradeoffs need evaluation on their eval set.

ashwin-eng: Ops suggestion: propose two commitment tiers in SOW: "Standard" = 5 reserved GPUs (AZ spread across 3 AZs if desired), autoscale cap 7 GPUs; "Lean" = 3 reserved GPUs + guaranteed burst credits to allow short spikes to 7. Lean depends on successful preheat and agreed latency SLAs.

maria-sales: good. Can you put numbers for estimated monthly baseline and a burst budget example so legal can get comfortable? Keep it one pager.

finance-bot: internal rates summary (internal only): reserved GPU seat = $3.10/hr. Burst-credit hourly-equivalent for short spikes ~ $1.10/hr when averaged. Monthly examples: Standard (5 GPUs): 5*24*30*3.10 = $11,160/mo base. Lean (3 GPUs): 3*24*30*3.10 = $6,696/mo base + burst spend variable. I'll draft a short table and drop into the deal folder.

priya-security: HIPAA notes: Private deployment is mandatory. We need customer-managed KMS (HSM recommended), explicit BAA, logging retention >= 1 year per their policy. Also call out: avoid spot instances for reserved plan; can offer spot for non-critical burst capacity only if they sign acceptance.

olivia-se: I'll take ops runbook. Suggested autoscale policy for the SOW: min_reserved = matches commitment (3 or 5), max = 7, scale aggressive for scale-up (detect sustained queue growth for 20s OR CPU > 70%) and conservative for scale-down (cooldown 3m). Preheat window: 10m before expected business peak.

olivia-se: preheat run checklist snippet ->
```
# preheat-run
1) run KV warmup for top 200 prefixes
2) bake kernels for seq_len 256 & 512
3) smoke load: 5m @ 300 RPS per GPU (or 75% of desired steady)
4) validate tail p95/p99 latency and token/s metrics
5) capture snapshot of KV hit rate
```

maria-sales: perfect. priya 1: what about AZ spread guidance? customer specifically asked about AZ isolation and eviction tolerance.

priya-security: For HIPAA we recommend AZ spread (e.g., 2/2/1) and avoid single-AZ single-point failures. If they require no spot eviction risk, commit to reserved/dedicated capacity. Document these options in SOW.

ashwin-eng: also note cold-starts: without preheat a spike could add 150-400ms tail latency while kernels warm up. Recommend we include preheat run as part of onboarding milestone and call out acceptance criteria.

deploy-bot: scheduled preheat smoke: 2024-06-12T08:30Z -> /infra/smoke-tests/1722223333. Ops oncall: @ashwin-eng.

maria-sales: can we get a one-pager by EOD with (a) Standard vs Lean commitment, (b) brief monthly cost numbers, (c) short security bullets and (d) preheat acceptance steps? I'll attach to SOW and ping legal.

finance-bot: will drop draft cost appendix in /deals/medisure/ by EOD.

olivia-se: I'll open ops handoff ticket and link the preheat checklist. Assigning to @ashwin-eng for execution.

ashwin-eng: I'll run the smoke tomorrow morning and paste results here. If the eval set tolerates quantized variant we'll push the Lean option as recommended to save them money.

maria-sales: thanks all 1: actionable. I'll update SOW and follow up after smoke. :thumbsup:
